SMALL CHANGES WHEN YOU SHOP You do not need to change everything at once to shop more responsibly. Start by choosing products with less (1) {#1}, such as fruit sold without an extra plastic wrapper. If you already have a suitable bag or box, bring it with you. These habits help (3) {#3} natural resources, including the water and trees used to produce paper products. Use available materials (4) {#4} rather than collecting more than you need. Some customers keep a folded shopping bag beside their front door, (5) {#5} makes it easier to remember the bag before leaving home. Some products still need protective packaging. (6) {#6}, we cannot remove every wrapper immediately. However, checking what you need and reusing what you already have are useful first steps.

answers.questionKey: part 2 — passage completion questions 13–17 read the following passage and choose the letter a, b, c, or d to indicate the option that best fits each numbered blank. this report examines unnecessary electricity and water use at a community language centre. it proposes practical improvements to the way its rooms and restrooms are managed. We therefore recommend delaying all action until every visitor agrees to the purchase of automatic lighting.C. We therefore recommend rebuilding the restrooms before taking any steps to repair the existing taps.Write A, B, C, or D - {#5}
